name: Lena — 250 hours behind her, about one flight a month now
summary: Years of flying and well over 200 hours, 70 or so of them thermic, several different sites, 10km cross-countries. But a new job and a young family mean about one flight a month and under 25 hours in the last year. Needs a new wing anyway and isn't sure what a C would actually change. Good judgement, honest about not having thought about goals lately.
why_this_persona: The 'experienced but no longer current' case, and the only persona exercising the widened currency gate. At mid-B to high-B the equivalent gate needs 'less than monthly'; here 'about monthly' qualifies too, because both figures anyone attaches to a first C are annual (50 and 70 hours a year) and monthly flying is a long way under either. She is also the test that the gate stays a combination: a pilot flying monthly with a strong 12-month total would NOT be capped.

notes: Computed skills 65.7, psychological 65.5, total 65.6, no bonus. Comfortably above the Nearly ready floor on score and above both Not yet category floors, so the single gate is what makes this Not yet — and the gate message is explicit that it is about how much she is flying right now rather than what she can do.

EXACTLY ONE GATE fires. 'occasional_pilot_profile' needs monthly-or-less flying AND under 25 hours in the last 12 months. The combination is the point: a pilot flying about monthly through a bad winter who put 60 hours in last season would NOT be capped. A synthetic unit check should confirm that, by changing airtime_last_12m to 50_80 and expecting Nearly ready.
'no_recent_flying' must NOT fire — she is still flying, just not much. That distinction is the reason the two currency gates exist separately.

'aspirational_rather_than_demonstrated' must NOT fire, and this is a deliberate near-miss worth preserving: her wing_limiting_evidence answer is 'I've wondered but couldn't point to a flight', and the gate's first clause requires the firmer 'not really'. She still gets the 'wing_hasnt_limited_you_yet' suggestion, which fires on both bands — so she is told the same thing without being capped for it twice.
'recurrency_plan' must NOT fire: its trigger is no flying at all in three months. 'improve_currency' is the right one for her, and the two share a topic so only one can ever be displayed.

'build_thermic_hours' fires on the 50-100 band deliberately, because that band straddles both published readings (75 and 100) and a pilot inside it may be short of either. Her result is not held by thermic hours — the band scores 0.6 and passes the Ready-blocker — but the suggestion is still accurate information.

'expectation_research' fires on 'I'm not really sure what would change', which is the most useful thing she could act on before spending money, and it pairs with 'resale_and_cost': her motive is 'I need a new wing anyway', which is the one motive that triggers the cost suggestion regardless of the result.

Her 'hasn't really come up' answer on the long-drive question scores 0.55 — neutral and low-information, like every other 'not come up' answer in this rubric. It must not be read as a fault and must not score as evidence either.
